From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 20:50:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Fwd: Spike in p99 and 500s affecting checkout (Stride)

Triage notes (initial, 20:50):
- Quick check of pod metrics and request latency traces shows sustained queue growth on the vcpu/gpu front-ends tied to a subset of long-context requests (avg seq len ~1200).
- Error 500s correlated with worker-side KV-cache eviction during high concurrency bursts; we see backpressure where prefetch queues saturate and timeouts bubble to 500.
- Concurrency cap for this routing is currently at 64 concurrent model streams; recent traffic pattern (more retries + longer sequences) increases effective work per token.

Immediate 1-hour mitigations (recommended):
- Temporarily raise concurrency cap to 96 for Stride routing (reduces queue buildup at front-end). Note: will increase peak GPU mem usage; ops to monitor.
- Enable aggressive per-account prefix KV caching for the 3 check endpoints to cut repeat token work.
- Short-term: route 15% of traffic to a warmed dedicated pool (dedicated-beta-7) with lower load to absorb bursts.

4-hour actions:
- Collect KV eviction traces and run targeted quantization profile for this model variant.
- Tune request-level circuit-breaker to fail fast for requests exceeding 2.5s on generation stage to avoid retries amplifying load.

24-hour actions:
- Investigate batching parameters and kernel selection for long sequence workloads; propose an optimized kernel set.
- Customer impact retro + SLA credit calc.

Attaching initial debug snippet: redwood_debug_trace_chunk_01.log and draft runbook mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf.

I'll execute the concurrency bump and the 15% routing now; will post monitoring links in 5–7m.

Dylan Brooks
SRE — Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:45:00 -0500
Subject: Action plan and status update — Stride checkout impact

Sarah — quick status and next steps after ops run the short mitigations:

What we did (completed):
- Raised concurrency cap from 64 -> 96 for Stride routing at 21:05 (Nov 1).
- Enabled aggressive per-account prefix KV caching for the three checkout endpoints at 21:12.
- Routed 15% of traffic to dedicated-beta-7 at 21:20; dedicated pool warmed and serving.

Immediate effect: p99 improved from ~1.8s -> ~1.1s within 7m of changes; 500s dropped by ~70% on the sample window. Full visible effect after 30m.

Open items / 4-hour plan (owners):
- (Dylan) Collect and share KV eviction traces and confirm whether we need a longer-term cache sizing change. ETA 4h.
- (Dylan) Tune circuit-breaker to fail-fast at generation stage for requests >2.5s. ETA 3h.
- (Neha) Hourly cadence with Stride PM + Ops for the next 6 hours; first checkpoint noon ET.
- (Markus) Prepare an executive note for Stride leadership including ETA for SLA credit calc and postmortem. ETA 24h.

We will keep the routing and higher cap for the next 6 hours while we assess cost and stability. If you want a short call now, happy to join — otherwise we'll post hourly updates here and share logs and the runbook.

Thanks — and apologies for the interruption during a ramp window. We'll follow up with a postmortem and proposed infra changes to prevent recurrence.

Neha Kapoor
